scope: Bounded same-workflow review of number_compute.py and output claims6–32, with priority exact checks6,8,23,32. Other output derivations were inspected for obvious scope/arithmetic errors; their computations were not rerun.

6.scope: The3302 classes descend AT STEP12 for all sufficiently large starts within the class. The794 others do not descend at that step; no eventual-orbit classification is implied. The parity itinerary is constant modulo4096 for12 one-division steps by induction.

8.verdict: confirmed from code inspection and exact comparison of stored totals
8.conclusion: All six weights beat unweighted prime-pair fractions but lose to the30-wheel baseline in both intervals. This is normalized weighted mass, not classifier accuracy or asymptotic prime detection.
8.scope: Did not recompute every divisor sum. Inspected Möbius coefficients, n(n+2) divisibility, squared common-denominator weights, prime-pair indicators, and matching interval endpoints; no error found.

23.proof: x^3−x+1 has no rational root and discriminant−23, giving S3≅GL2(F2). The second cubic factors (x−1)(x²+x−1), with quadratic discriminant5, giving the order-two point stabilizer.
23.scope: These are group-image fractions. Frobenius interpretations require odd good primes (exclude2,23 for E1 and2,5 for E2). No higher-modulus independence follows.

32.verdict: confirmed with independent rational interval recomputation
32.conclusion: The saved4096-bit prefix is certified by equal scaled floors. The exact one-bit discrepancy increase disproves monotone doubling for this prefix, not normality.
32.method: Reverse-Horner evaluation of rational alternating arctangent partial sums and explicit next-term bounds, followed by Machin interval combination.

wording_cautions: In item6 use eventually-descending-in-class only to mean sufficiently large starts descend at step12; the classification is not eventual convergence.
Item23 group fractions should not be confused with finite prime-count proportions; Frobenius assertions exclude odd bad primes and prime2.
